title: Capacity orientation microflows and autoscale explainer visuals for Dedicated onboarding
creator: Lina Chen
description: Create a compact, accessible set of visuals and microflow animations for the Dedicated onboarding quickstart. These assets should explain capacity setup, autoscaling behavior (scale-up/scale-down/opportunistic burst), and a concise SLA tradeoff overview. Aim for a single-page hero flow for the console quickstart, two doc-oriented explainer illustrations (print-ready), three looping micro-interaction GIFs showing autoscale transitions, and a small set of responsive screenshots for the release notes. Assets must include export-ready variants (SVG/PNG/GIF) and copy alternatives for localization.
deliverables: Hero canvas: 5 frames (desktop+mobile variants) showing initial capacity selection -> baseline pool -> autoscale event -> burst fallback -> SLA notification
Two doc illustrations: (1) Autoscale decision tree infographic, (2) SLA cost vs latency quadrant diagram
Three microflow GIFs: (a) smooth scale-up, (b) gradual scale-down with cache reuse, (c) fallback to cheaper model variant on capacity pressure
Console screenshots: 6 annotated images for docs and in-app help (with redlines)
Asset package: SVG source files, PNG export at 2x, GIFs under 1.2MB, copy variants (EN/ES/FR), and alt-text for each asset
acceptance_criteria: Design sign-off from PM (Sofia Patel) and Eng lead (Oliver Brooks)
Assets exported and uploaded to Drive folder: /Shared/Design/dedicated-onboarding/CapOrient_2025
Animations tested in staging console and replay at target 24fps without >150ms frame drops
Illustrations reviewed for accessibility (WCAG color contrast >= 4.5:1) and have alt-text entries
Handoff tokens and redlines added to Figma file; engineering tasks created for screenshot capture and CSS animation implementation
design_notes: Target tone: concise, technical-friendly, avoids marketing fluff — focus on developer decision points
Use existing Redwood design tokens and updated color palette from design-system v3
Microflow animations should be looped at 1.5–2s per state; prefer morphing shapes over heavy motion
SLA quadrant should show three example personas (startup, mid-market, enterprise) with recommended capacity profiles
Provide a low-bandwidth static alternative for the doc site (single composite PNG) and inline SVGs for console
